text: Beside the earlier promise, the seeming difference is reduced. Isaac is the child of the covenant, the one through whom the nations are to be blessed; in Genesis 22 that promise has become a test. The scene depends on one word, *hineni*, "here I am," spoken by Abraham three times: to God, to Isaac, and to the angel. It is not the same word when it returns. Each return exacts more. The language of presence has become also the language of something not yet named, and there the sentence breaks off.
